questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Whether I could speak the language in the country and whether the host university could guarantee housing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, University of Leeds was very good at sending information via emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many dorms were available, and I was assigned a dorm with private ensuite bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a shared kitchen with 5 other exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's great, close too class and social events taking place on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to send proof of enrollment at University of Copenhagen and English language proficiency, which was my high school grades, and a picture of my scanned passport. Once I was accepted, I could register for specific classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email both University of Leeds and University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got a spot at all the modules I had applied for, but I ended up changing one of the modules because it did not suit me as well as I thought.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the emails you receive thoroughly and write them as many emails as you need - don't be afraid to ask 'dumb' questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three modules; one was a second year bachelor level module in the School of English; one was a third year bachelor level module in the School of English; and one was discovery module from the Language Centre.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar with lectures and seminars, though both were shorter sessions than those of UCPH. Lectures were 1 hour and seminars were between 1 and 2 hours. Some modules only had seminars - and some had additional field trips.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ELU2010 Language Through Literature and Place: Reading Yorkshire (39798)
ENGL2030 Writing Environments: Literature, Nature, Culture (39506)
ENGL3046 Parts, Periodicals, Newspapers: Literature and the Nineteenth-Century Press  (40346)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all, but I found ELU2010 Language Through Literature and Place: Reading Yorkshire (39798) especially interesting because it centered around literature that was written or takes place in Yorkshire, and we went on field trips to explore Leeds, which was very informative and immersive.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I got a meningitis vaccine when I arrived that cost 900 DKK, because there was a little card on my desk in my dorm that said "Meningitis Kills" and strongly advised me to get one - that had not been clear from the university's email correspondence.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and tea in cafe's are much cheaper over there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were over 300 societies I could become a member of that had all kinds of activities and socials. I was part of the book club, the English society and the art society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the society fair in the first week of the semester and see which society fits your interests.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit Haworth where the Brontë-sisters lived.
Visit London.
Visit Edinburgh.
Visit the Lake District.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The people in Leeds are very kind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get involved in the societies - many local students are part of them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find unscented products for personal hygiene.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the people - everyone called each other "luv" and "darling".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the society fair at the start of the semester.
Try to get accommodation on campus - many activities take place in Leeds University Union which is on campus.
Enjoy all the libraries.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Beware of the fact that the University of Leeds only provide provisional grades - the final grades are set in June and might cause problems with graduation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and going on an adventure alone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first day was hard, where everything is new, but as soon as that first day was over it was great.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
